_: Written by `ci-video narrate`. Records which line each mp3 is a read of, in which voice, on which engine, at what prosody — so a later edit to any of those can be detected instead of silently keeping the old recording. Commit this with the mp3s.

app-privacy.text: Every app page carries an App Privacy card, and where nobody has declared anything, it says so.

open.text: Four hundred and ninety apps, each one running on hardware you own.

sign-in.text: It opens on a local login. Signing in anywhere else is optional.

pair-the-hub.text: A new Hub asks for one pairing code from Companion Portal.

first-boot.text: First boot is one pass. Local models, network, apps.

home-dashboard.text: This is home. Disk, CPU and memory, read off hardware you own.

browse-the-store.text: The store is fed by the open Hub market. Search, or browse.

open-alternatives.text: For the software you rent, the store names the open replacement you can own.

configure-install.text: Secrets generate themselves. Everything else an app asks for, you see before it runs.

install-and-run.text: When the badge turns green, the app is live on your own machine.

bring-your-own-app.text: Your own containers become a first class app, with a name and an address.

expose-a-port.text: Anything already running here gets a name, a certificate, and a door you choose.

local-models.text: The Hub reads your hardware and picks models it can actually run at home.

own-your-agents.text: Agents drive your Hub through tools you can read, scoped by keys you issue.

every-dial.text: Want the dials? They are all here. Reading your own logs costs nothing.

recap.text: Your hardware, your domain, your data. Nothing to cancel.

second-job.text: You wanted a home server. What you got was a second job.

the-list.text: Install the OS. Find the apps. Configure the apps.

the-longer-list.text: Open a port, and hope. Build a VPN. Learn what a reverse proxy is. Learn what a certificate is. Learn why it broke.

most-people-quit.text: Most people quit right about here.

title.text: There is a much shorter way.

any-computer.text: Any computer already sitting around. The old gaming rig. The laptop in the closet. Windows, Mac, Linux, it does not matter.

reads-the-machine.text: Companion Hub reads the machine. CPU, GPU, memory, storage.

picks-the-models.text: Then it tunes itself to the hardware that is actually there, and picks models that run fast on it, not models that melt it.

apps-arrive.text: Apps arrive already configured. Already private.

from-a-phone.text: Reachable from a phone, without putting anything on the open internet.

hermes-openclaw.text: Hermes runs locally. OpenClaw takes the boring parts of the day.

alternatives.text: Every service worth renting, beside the version worth owning.

the-things-stay.text: The files stay in the house. The work stays in the office. The photos stay in the room where they were taken.

ci-hub-30-second-job.text: You wanted a home server. You got a second job.

ci-hub-30-the-longer-list.text: Open a port. Build a VPN. Learn what a reverse proxy is.

ci-hub-30-reads-the-machine.text: Companion Hub reads your hardware, and tunes itself to it.

ci-hub-30-the-things-stay.text: The files stay in the house. The photos stay in the room.

ci-hub-bumper-laptop-line.text: That old laptop is a server now.

ci-hub-bumper-renting-line.text: Stop renting what could be owned.

ci-hub-bumper-landlord-line.text: Local AI, one roof, no landlord.

ci-hub-30-title.text: There is a much shorter way. One installer, one wizard.
